findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "screen" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: domain, url, email, phone, company_name, context, amount, policy, country, ip_country, ip_region, ip_asn, browser_timezone, stated_country, signal, site

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: qualify_counterparty, screen, check_email · Private data: search_business, get_business_file, qualify_counterparty · Public sink: screen, check_email · Destructive: qualify_counterparty, screen.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: qualify_counterparty, screen, check_email · Private data: search_business, get_business_file, qualify_counterparty · Public sink: screen, check_email · Destructive: qualify_counterparty, screen

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_business" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
